entries.subject: DAMIT 172: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-172.txt. Model 172, version 2011-03-28, pole (249°, -68°), period 13.06133 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 44 ±15 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.finding: [B. D. Warner (2008), Shape and spin models for four asteroids](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2008MPBu...35..167W) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the documented physical calibration supplies the selected scale. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 38.36 ± 0.46 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 167 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.finding: [Ďurech et al. (2011), occultation silhouette scaling](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1104.4227) — retained primary publication; see the body-specific selection and calibration above.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 171, pole ['107', '-69'], [Model 171](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/171) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 171: pole (107°, -69°), 13.06133 h, version 2011-03-28, archive diameter 51 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.
